note: Forest Service campground in the Little Missouri National Grassland badlands, 33 miles southwest of Watford City beside paved ND-16. Three camping loops along the lake, each site with a roofed picnic shelter; the boat dock and floating fishing pier are in the separate day-use loop. The hand pump's water is seasonal and the Forest Service page said it was off in November 2026. --Claude
summary: USFS page + rec.gov read: open, 18 FCFS sites in 3 loops, $10, 14-day limit, no hookups, pads to 60 ft, year-round with limited services outside Memorial Day-Labor Day, Senior/Access 50%. Groups now manual; note corrected (SW not NW of Watford City; access is paved ND-16, not gravel). Pin on the day-use lot ~530 m from the camping loops. Lakeview stands (upgrade lead, no site numbers).
flags: PIN: stored 47.67370,-103.81150 (= the FS page's point) sits on the day-use parking lot / boat-ramp loop north of the campground, not on campsites. The three camping loops: west loop (6 shelters along the lake arm) centred ~47.6690,-103.8104; NE loop across the bay ~47.6728,-103.8058; south loop ~47.6655,-103.8087. Propose moving the pin to the west (main) loop 47.6690,-103.8104 (~530 m). rec.gov's facility point 47.667627,-103.81103 sits between the west and south loops.

WATERFRONT: lakeview stands; possible LAKEFRONT upgrade lead for the reviewer. On Esri imagery three west-loop shelters sit ~13-35 m from the lake arm (shelters at ~47.6695,-103.8102, ~47.6686,-103.8104 and ~47.6676,-103.8102; the arm is ~40-65 m wide and part of a lake well over 5 acres). The northern one is over open grass/rush fringe; the other two have a shrub band between. FS photo 05092025-FS-SCM-104 shows a site shelter on open grass at the water's edge. But neither the FS nor rec.gov publishes site numbers or a site map (the rec.gov catalog has no per-site coordinates), so no site can be named; per the rules, no upgrade proposed. The south loop's sites sit by a narrow tree-lined inlet (creek-sized).

WATER: conflicting official statements. The FS page says 'Potable water is not available at this site. Water is not currently available at this site.' while its intro and rec.gov describe a hand pump ('Water is available Memorial day to Labor day'). potable_water left unset.

FIT/ACCESS: pads average 50 ft, to 60 ft (FS). The campground sits directly on paved ND-16; the stored note's 'Gravel-road access' is wrong (only the campground loops are gravel). No FS road warning, no alert for Sather Lake.
PHONE: stored empty -> 701-842-8500 (McKenzie Ranger District, on the FS page and rec.gov). WEBSITE: keep both (FS page; rec.gov listing is information only, 'no reservable sites').

HORSES (AWH rule 2026-11-12): the FS Sather Lake page's only horse wording is a 'Horse Riding and Camping' opportunity heading linking to 'Horseback Riding', with no text; it names no horse sites, corrals or hitch rails and no horse rule. The rec.gov listing is silent. Imagery of the three loops showed no corrals or horse pens. Agency silent on horse facilities -> not a horse campground; keep.
